chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'News of one of my companions has reached me from Al-Awas, and that was during the month of Ramadan. Should I go to meet him and break (my fast)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Should I go to meet him and break (my fast), or should I stay and fast?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go to meet him and break (your fast).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking the fast when traveling to meet a companion in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a traveler who receives news of a companion's arrival in Al-Awṣa during Ramadan is permitted to break their fast to go meet them, prioritizing the social obligation of greeting over the strict continuity of fasting. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding *safar* (travel), where the act of traveling itself, even for social purposes, validates the concession of *qasr* and *iftar*, provided the traveler does not remain stationary in one place. The specific mention of Al-Awṣa, a known location near Kufa, grounds this legal principle in the historical context of early Shia community interactions.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There came to me news of my companions from Al-Awas, and that was during a Month of Ramazan. Shall I meet him and break (the Fast)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Shall I meet him and break, or shall I say and Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Meet him, and break’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one of my friends who has come to al- ’A‘was in the month of Ramadan; if I can go to meet him and stop fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Should I go to meet him and stop fasting or stay home and fast?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You should go to meet him and stop fasting.’”
